verdict.rationale: Smithery's build docs describe a real publishing flow: publish a deployed server by URL, distribute local stdio servers as MCPB bundles, and get a dedicated server page where users can discover and install it. However, the first-party shutdown notice says accounts, API keys, and the CLI stopped working on October 31, 2026, and the docs tree was removed. Smithery remains only as a public, non-proxied registry, so it is unclear whether developers can still publish. Missing for 10: confirmation that publishing works after the shutdown given that accounts are discontinued, current documentation of the publishing flow, and independent hands-on corroboration of publishing.

support.subject: As a developer, I can publish my own MCP server on the platform for distribution, discovery, and installation by others

citations.quote: If you’ve already deployed an MCP server elsewhere, you can publish it directly on Smithery via the URL method.
Distribution — Get a dedicated server page where users can discover, try, and install your MCP from any client
For local stdio servers — Smithery distributes a pre-built MCPB bundle that clients download and run locally.
Smithery will remain as a public (non-proxied) MCP registry.
